title: Torcolo di San Costanzo
author: Marco Bellini
desc: Perugia's traditional ring-shaped cake, studded with candied fruit, raisins, and pine nuts, baked each year to honor the city's patron saint on January 29th.
longDesc: Torcolo takes its name from its twisted ring shape, and though it is now available year-round in Perugia's bakeries, its deepest ties remain to the annual feast of San Costanzo, when the cake is traditionally shared among family and friends.
ingredients: Pearl sugar or coarse sugar, for topping
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the warm milk with a pinch of sugar and let sit for 5 minutes.
Combine the flour, remaining sugar, eggs, and citrus zest, then add the yeast mixture, kneading into a smooth dough.
Gradually work in the softened butter until fully incorporated.
Let rise, covered, in a warm place for about 2 hours, until doubled.
Fold in the candied fruit, drained raisins, and pine nuts.
Shape the dough into a ring and place in a well-oiled ring-shaped pan.
Scatter with pearl sugar before baking.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 25–30 minutes until deeply golden.
chefTips: A ring-shaped pan gives the traditional torcolo shape, though it can also be shaped freehand into a ring on a baking sheet.
Work the butter in gradually for the smoothest, most elastic dough.
This cake is traditionally shared each January 29th for the feast of Perugia's patron saint.
commonMistakes: Underproofing the dough, resulting in a denser cake rather than the traditional light, airy crumb.
Overloading with candied fruit, which can weigh down the delicate dough.
Skipping the pearl sugar topping, which is a traditional decorative and textural element.
storage: Store wrapped at room temperature for up to 4 days.
reheating: Not applicable; served at room temperature.
healthBenefits: A source of protein from the eggs, best enjoyed as an occasional festive treat.
culturalNote: Torcolo di San Costanzo is deeply tied to Perugia's annual celebration of its patron saint each January 29th, though the cake has since become a year-round favorite in local bakeries.
